scope: Independent test-sufficiency review of all-30 runtime replay and narrow language error counterparts; not completed feature or production approval
assessment: All thirty immutable reference IDs are parameterized, with exhaustive actual Java setup and a failing default for unknown IDs; no ignored or expected-failure cases. Inputs alone are read from reference for execution.

RuntimeReplay records actual response, essential headers, handler order, pathParams, path/url/baseUrl/originalUrl, completion state and handled Throwables. Initial handler return and owned callback futures are joined before snapshots, avoiding lost after-response trace.
The two registration error cases execute real registration and compare failures without manufacturing requests. Missing future APIs throw explicit AssertionErrors rather than synthetic success.

Counterparts are restricted by case ID and actual Throwable family; only exact terminal help URL omission is allowed for registration. Raw Throwable class/message JSON is cross-checked. Decode status400/raw value and deliberately thrown exact RuntimeException messages remain checked.

Strict comparator retains response/body/header/trace/parameter/completion comparisons. Negative controls cover wrong error families, meaningful reason/index/source/message/raw-value changes, wrong status, forged error metadata, body/header/status/trace differences, parameter absence/null/list shape, and stale provenance.
Diff from d84ca92 changes six parity tests/docs files only; raw generator, corpus, lock, dependencies and production source remain unchanged.
limitations: In-memory replay does not establish TinyHttpd/Servlet socket normalization. Five actual runtime failures must be resolved by relevant core implementation before whole-feature parity is claimed. Review stops at first PASS; no additional Gradle execution needed for the preserved stable evidence.
